subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Hydraulic Brakes: Stopping Cars Safely
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Hydraulic Brakes: Stopping Cars Safely.

hook.text: Press the brake pedal and four wheels stop simultaneously. Hydraulic fluid carries your foot pressure to every caliper.

buildup.text: A master cylinder converts pedal force into fluid pressure. Brake lines carry that pressure to calipers at each wheel.

discovery.text: The calipers squeeze pads against rotors. Friction converts kinetic energy into heat. The car slows down.

twist.text: ABS pumps the brakes 15 times per second during a skid. Hydraulic valves release and reapply pressure faster than any foot.

climax.text: Dual circuits ensure that if one brake line leaks, the other two wheels still stop the car. Redundancy saves lives.

punchline.text: Your foot pushes fluid. Fluid pushes pads. Pads stop tons of steel.

quiz.question: Why do car brake systems use dual hydraulic circuits?
options: To provide stronger braking force on the front wheels than the rear
So that if one circuit leaks, the remaining circuit can still stop the car
To allow the driver to brake the front and rear independently
